subject: Clarifying QPS & P95 needs to recommend Hosted vs Dedicated
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Clarifying QPS & P95 needs to recommend Hosted vs Dedicated

Hi Samir / Olivia —

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful to see FastRetail's checkout flow and traffic patterns. To make a crisp recommendation between Hosted API and Dedicated capacity (and whether Private is needed down the line), we need a short set of concrete numbers from your infra team:

- Sustained QPS during peak 10-min windows (average and max)
- Expected burst QPS (short spikes) and frequency (e.g., holiday peaks)
- Target latency SLO (p50, p95) for the checkout path and a lower-priority analytics path
- Number of concurrent model variants (are you serving a single model or multiple ensembles?)

If you can share the above, we can: (1) map to a capacity profile (e.g., Dedicated 4xA100 vs Hosted with caching/config), (2) run a 2-week pilot benchmark, and (3) provide an estimated committed-cost vs pay-as-you-go comparison.

I pulled together a short benchmark plan and a pilot scope we typically use — attaching for reference.

Proposed immediate next step: if you can paste numbers for the bullets above, Marcus and I will convert that into a recommended deployment path and a pilot quote by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Thanks Laura — quick answers from our side (put together with infra):
- Sustained QPS (checkout): average 60 QPS during peak 10-min windows, sustained max observed 180 QPS for 3–7 min bursts.
- Burst pattern: we get short spikes up to ~220 QPS a few times per day (30–90s), plus seasonal spikes expected x2 during promotions.
- Latency SLO (checkout): strict p95 target is 350ms end-to-end (model inference target ~200ms). Analytics path can tolerate p95 up to 1s.
- Model variants: single core generator model for checkout, but we also run an auxiliary reranker for recommendations (so 2 models served concurrently).

We prefer Hosted for speed to production, but worried about consistent p95 under the sustained 60–180 QPS pattern. Happy to run a pilot.

—Samir

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarifying QPS & P95 needs to recommend Hosted vs Dedicated

Laura — thanks for the context and Samir for the numbers. TL;DR recommendation below, followed by rationale and requested clarifications.

Recommendation (initial): Dedicated capacity pilot.
- Rationale: FastRetail has sustained peak averages (~60 QPS) with multi-minute bursts to ~180 QPS and a tight p95 target (350ms client-side, ~200ms inference). Dedicated provides predictable tail-latency and reserved GPU memory for KV caches; it's typically the safe path when sustained p50/p95 and multi-model concurrency matter.
- Hosted could work if you (a) accept slightly looser p95 under sustained bursts and (b) we implement aggressive KV prefix caching + autoscale tiering. For short-term evaluation Hosted + caching is faster to deploy but may risk tail latencies during sustained bursts.

Sizing note (back-of-envelope): to hit ~200ms model inference p95 for a 70B-ish decoder on A100-class hardware under 60–180 QPS concurrent with a reranker, we expect a 3–4 GPU Dedicated pool (4xA100 recommended for pilot). We'll run a focused load test that reproduces your 10-min sustained window + 220 QPS spikes.

Action items / clarifying questions for Samir / infra:
1) Can you share 1–2 representative request payload sizes (average token length) and typical max sequence length?
2) Any hard network egress constraints we should know about (VPC only, static IPs)?
3) Are you comfortable starting with a 2-week Dedicated pilot (reserved infra) so we can collect stable p95 measurements, or do you want to try Hosted first?

I'll attach the benchmark plan and a pilot-scope CSV with the reference configs I mentioned. If Laura approves, I'll draft a short pilot quote (hours + reserved capacity & monitoring) and a canary rollback plan.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin

Samir —

Thanks — that clarifies a lot. Based on Marcus's recommendation and your constraints, I propose the following immediate plan:

1) 2-week Dedicated pilot (4xA100) to measure stable p95 under your 10-min sustained windows + synthetic 220 QPS spike runs.
2) Redwood will run the benchmark scripts (attached) and provide a short report with p50/p95/p99 graphs and recommendations on batching/cache config.
3) If pilot meets your p95 target, we will convert to a Reserved Dedicated commitment (we'll include a few burst slots for promotional days).

I've attached the benchmark plan and pilot scope. If that looks good, I'll: (a) open a HubSpot deal with quoted pilot cost, (b) send a short DocuSign for the pilot terms, and (c) schedule an infra sync to collect payload samples and static IP info.

Proposed timeline: pilot starts as early as next Monday (16 Aug) if we sign by EOD this week.

Let me know if you'd prefer Hosted-first and a shorter smoke test instead — we can pivot.

Thanks,
